page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, paired with 2,832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The hardware architecture features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and AES-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core and multi-core computational throughput. The instance ranks in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems for Geekbench single-core performance (2,808.0) and multi-core performance (24,409.0), as well as stress-ng single-core processing. Cryptographic and compression metrics also place in the upper tier, highlighted by 41.54 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In-memory operations show consistent execution, processing 78.13 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining uncached large-block write memory bandwidth of 103.08 GB/sec.

Equipped with 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and zero onboard GPUs, the configuration balances large active working sets with fast local scratch data access. The heavy allocation of memory relative to vCPUs provides an efficient operational footprint for dense data environments, avoiding the compute waste common when scaling memory-bound workloads on general-purpose instances.

Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is suitable for high-throughput in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, real-time analytics engines, data transformations, and CPU-based natural language processing inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor reaching 4.5 GHz. Configured with 384.0 GB of RAM and 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs, the instance delivers a balanced 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio alongside high-speed scratch storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier computational capabilities, scoring 2,808.0 in Geekbench single-core, 24,409.0 in multi-core, and handling 78.13 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware acceleration is supported via AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. This configuration offers solid cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by supplying substantial memory density without requiring unneeded compute expansion. It is suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caches, distributed analytics, and large compilation workflows.
